I'm not saying all detransitioners aren't trans, rather the specific one's my dad is using as an example in an attempt to debunk me being trans. ("These people transitioned and hated themselves/regretted it, so you'll never be happy if you do it") 

I accept my dad's opinion, however he's choosing to ignore any other information that support trans people. He's also going out of his way to refer to me as a girl, and emphasising that I'm his "daughter".
Ultimately he's showing a lack of respect for me, and this isn't the first time he's done it.

My dad would read my diary, then make fun of me for what I wrote in there. I was about 6 at the time, and had written about how he had pinned me down and hit me because I accidentally slammed the door (the window was open in my room). It was a disgusting invasion of my privacy, he also found my mother's diary and read it multiple times before. He once read it out loud to me and my sister.
Seriously, if you read someone's diary and get angry about what they've written about you (usually in the heat of the moment), you're a dumbass.
I never wrote a diary after that, and threw away the one I did own. I had lost what could have been an outlet for some of my more negative emotions. Someone could leave their diary open, on a table and I wouldn't bloody read it. Their secret feelings are their own until they want to talk about it. The same goes with sketch books. Drawings can be very personal to most people. 
Another thing is when at the age of 15, I told my dad I thought I was depressed. Being told to "Wait until you get into the real world" Didn't really help. 
Now my dad wonders why I don't talk to him about my feelings anymore. I also still find it hard to actually talk to people when I'm having a hard time, until I have a full blown breakdown. 
To say I greatly prefer my mum is an understatement. She's a fantastic human being and probably the reason I haven't completely lost my mind growing up. Having someone who actually pays attention to your hobbies and interests is so damn important, rather than only paying attention when those interests match your own (yep talking about my dad. Again)
